How to Clean Out After the Holidays

The holiday season is over, and now it's time to tackle the mess that's left behind. From wrapping paper and decorations to broken toys and unwanted gifts, the aftermath of the holidays can be overwhelming. At 1-800-GOT-JUNK?, we're here to help you clean out after the holidays and get your home back in order.

Before You Start Cleaning

Before you begin cleaning out after the holidays, take a moment to assess the situation. Walk through your home and make a list of the areas that need the most attention. This will help you create a plan of attack and ensure that you don't miss any important tasks.

Consider enlisting the help of family members or friends to make the task more manageable. Sorting and Purging

Once you have a plan in place, it's time to start sorting and purging. Go through each room in your home and separate items into three piles: keep, donate/sell, and throw away. Be ruthless – if you don't need it or love it, consider getting rid of it.

Here are some tips to keep in mind as you sort and purge:

  • Consider the 80/20 rule: 80% of the time, you likely only use 20% of your belongings.
  • Let go of items that are broken or no longer serve a purpose.
  • Keep items that bring you joy or serve a functional purpose.

Organizing Your Space

Once you've purged your unwanted items, it's time to organize your space. This will help you create a more peaceful and functional living environment.

Here are some tips to keep in mind as you organize:

  • Use storage containers to keep clutter at bay.
  • Label your storage containers so you can easily find what you need.
  • Consider investing in a shelving unit or other organizational system.

And, if you're feeling overwhelmed, consider enlisting the help of a professional organizer. They can help you create a customized organizational system that meets your needs and fits your lifestyle.

Donating and Recycling

As you clean out after the holidays, you may come across items that are still in good condition but no longer needed or wanted. Consider donating these items to a local charity or thrift store.

Here are some tips to keep in mind when donating:

  • Make sure the item is in good condition and still has a useful life.
  • Research the charity or thrift store to ensure they accept the type of item you're donating.
  • Get a receipt for your donation, as it may be tax deductible.

And, if you have items that can't be donated, consider recycling them. Many communities have recycling programs for items like electronics, batteries, and paper products.

Final Touches

Once you've cleaned out after the holidays, it's time to put the finishing touches on your space. Take a moment to tidy up, vacuum, and dust. This will help you feel more relaxed and at peace in your home.

Here are some final tips to keep in mind:

  • Take care of any lingering tasks, like cleaning the fridge or oven.
  • Consider hosting a post-holiday party to show off your newly cleaned and organized space.
  • Make a plan to maintain your space throughout the year, so you don't have to deal with a big cleanup again.
